hints: Focus on each $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group separately, remember a primary alcohol oxidises in two stages, first to an aldehyde then to a carboxylic acid.
Start by listing what happens if you oxidise only one end while the other end stays as $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, then think about oxidising both ends together.
Write out all five combinations of $\text{-CHO}$ and $\text{-COOH}$ on the two carbons, then add up how many of each group appear across the whole set.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidation of primary alcohols**

Think gently about what each end can become. A primary $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group oxidises first to $\text{-CHO}$ and then further to $\text{-COOH}$.

$$\text{-CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{-CHO} \rightarrow \text{-COOH}$$

**List oxidation on one side only**

Keep the C-C bond intact and oxidise just one carbon. This gives two different products.

$$\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CHO (1 x -CHO)}$$ $$\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-COOH (1 x -COOH)}$$

**List oxidation on both sides**

Now oxidise both carbons at the same time. Each side can be $\text{-CHO}$ or $\text{-COOH}$, giving three more products.

$$\text{OHC-CHO (2 x -CHO)}$$ $$\text{OHC-COOH (1 x -CHO, 1 x -COOH)}$$ $$\text{HOOC-COOH (2 x -COOH)}$$

**Add up the totals**

Count all the aldehyde groups across the five structures, then all the acid groups.

$$\text{Total -CHO} = 1 + 0 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 4$$ $$\text{Total -COOH} = 0 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 4$$

options.A: Incorrect. 3 and 3 is too low because it misses one aldehyde and one acid. Students often forget the mixed product $\text{OHC-COOH}$ which contributes one of each, or miscount the dialdehyde and diacid.
options.B: Incorrect. The acid total of 4 is right, but 3 aldehydes is one short. This usually happens if you miss that $\text{OHC-CHO}$ has two $\text{-CHO}$ groups, not one.
options.C: Incorrect. The aldehyde total of 4 is right, but 3 acids is one short. This usually happens if you miss that $\text{HOOC-COOH}$ has two $\text{-COOH}$ groups, not one.
options.D: Correct. The five products are $\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$, $\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, $\text{OHC-CHO}$, $\text{OHC-COOH}$ and $\text{HOOC-COOH}$. Adding across all five gives 4 $\text{-CHO}$ groups and 4 $\text{-COOH}$ groups.
